# Ticket Flow — full agent context

Source of truth for humans: https://smg99.github.io/ticket-flow/
Machine signposts: /llm.txt · /llms.txt · this file
Repository: https://github.com/smg99/ticket-flow
Companion playbook: https://smg99.github.io/engineering-ai-playbook/

## Definition

Ticket Flow is a free, public, thin orchestration layer for IDE agents (especially Cursor). It sequences work after a real ticket ID exists: fetch the issue, create a scoped branch, implement with tests, stop for human Confirm before commit, stop again before push/PR, then optionally ask before chat notify. It ships as a skill, always-applied rules, and thin shell wrappers—not as a SaaS product. The public website only displays guidance; it never fetches tickets, runs agents, commits code, or posts to chat.

## Not this

- Not a replacement for the AI-Assisted SDLC Playbook (use the playbook for vague requirements → stories)
- Not automatic Jira/Linear/GitHub ticket creation
- Not a hosted runner that opens PRs for you
- Not permission to paste proprietary code or secrets into public chat or this repo

## When to use it

1. Stories already exist as real tickets in your tracker.
2. You are in an agentic IDE with the product repo (and optionally this skill) available.
3. Pair with playbook stage “Develop one story” for planning prompts; use Ticket Flow for the ticket → PR sequence and gates.

## Hard rules (must not deviate)

1. Confirm before every commit and before every PR. Silence is not Confirm.
2. Never mention AI, Cursor, or agents in commits, PR titles, or descriptions.
3. Stage only ticket-relevant files (path-scoped; no git add -A).
4. Reproduce UI bugs in the running app before calling the fix done.
5. Prefer root-cause fixes; assert failure modes in tests.
6. Tests ship with the change unless the user explicitly waives them.
7. Ask before chat notify; never invent a default channel.
8. Never force-push protected defaults (main/master); never push secrets.
9. On script failure: report the error—do not invent workarounds or fake success.

## Flow steps

1. Queue & progress — `.local/progress.md` from docs/progress-template.md
2. Fetch issue — `./scripts/issue-get.sh` (must be configured; no invented ticket text)
3. Branch — `bugfix/ID` or `feature/ID` via `./scripts/git-branch.sh`
4. Implement & test — project rules; UI reproduce when needed
5. Confirm before commit — Impact Area summary; wait for explicit Confirm
6. Stage & commit — `./scripts/git-commit.sh "ID: why-message"`
7. Confirm before PR — title + Impact Area body + test plan
8. Push & PR — `./scripts/git-push.sh` then `./scripts/git-pr.sh`
9. Ask before chat — Yes/No + channel; `./scripts/notify-chat.sh` only if configured
10. Close out — mark Done; optional consumer package bump with the same gates

## Impact Area template

- App
- Surfaces
- Components / APIs
- Regression Risk
- Tests

## Naming glossary

- Primary app — main product repo only
- Product suite — primary app + sibling product repos
- Suite + shared UI — those products plus the shared UI package (shared UI is neither “the app” nor “the suite”)

## Security boundary

Public site and repo: generic guidance and synthetic examples only. Real tickets, code, credentials, and client operational data stay in approved private systems.

## Docs map

- docs/ticket-flow-agent-guide.md — full team guide
- docs/progress-template.md — local queue template
- docs/CONTRIBUTING.md — how to extend
- .cursor/skills/ticket-flow/SKILL.md — agent checklist
- assets/flow-data.js — site step copy (keep aligned with the skill)
